You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

% tuc(1) Tuc 1.3.0 | Tuc Manual
%
% Sep 10, 2025

NAME
====

**tuc** — cut text or bytes and keep what you need

SYNOPSIS
========

| **tuc** \[FLAGS]... \[OPTIONS]... \< input
| **tuc** \[FLAGS]... \[OPTIONS]... filepath

DESCRIPTION
===========

Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts.  

FLAGS
=====

-g, \--greedy-delimiter
:   Match consecutive delimiters as if it was one

-p, \--compress-delimiter
:   Print only the first delimiter of a sequence

-s, \--only-delimited
:   Print only lines containing the delimiter

-V, \--version
:   Print version information

-z, \--zero-terminated
:   Line delimiter is NUL (\0), not LF (\\n)

-h, \--help
:   Print this help and exit

-m, \--complement
:   Invert fields (e.g. \'2\' becomes \'1,3:\')

-j, \--(no-)join
:   Print selected parts with delimiter in between

\--json
:   Print fields as a JSON array of strings

\--no-mmap
:   Disable memory mapping

OPTIONS
=======

| **-f**, **\--fields** [bounds]
|        Fields to keep, 1-indexed, comma separated.
|        Use colon (:) to match a range (inclusive).
|        Use equal (=) to apply out of bound fallback.
|        Fields can be negative (-1 is the last field).

|        [default 1:]

|        e.g. cutting the string \'a-b-c-d\' on \'-\'
|          `-f 1     => a`
|          `-f 1:    => a-b-c-d`
|          `-f 1:3   => a-b-c`
|          `-f 3,2   => cb`
|          `-f 3,1:2 => ca-b`
|          `-f -3:-2 => b-c`
|          `-f 1,8=fallback => afallback`

|        To re-apply the delimiter add -j, to replace
|        it add -r (followed by the new delimiter)

|        You can also format the output using {} syntax
|        e.g.
|          `-f '({1}, {2})' => (a, b)`

|        You can escape { and } using {{ and }}.

| **-b**, **\--bytes** [bounds]
|        Same as \--fields, but it keeps bytes

| **-c**, **\--characters** [bounds]
|        Same as \--fields, but it keeps characters

| **-l**, **\--lines** [bounds]
|        Same as \--fields, but it keeps lines
|        Implies \--join. To merge lines, use \--no-join

| **-d**, **\--delimiter** [delimiter]
|        Delimiter used by \--fields to cut the text
|        [default: \\t]

| **-e**, **\--regex** [some regex]
|        Use a regular expression as delimiter

| **-r**, **\--replace-delimiter** [new delimiter]
|        Replace the delimiter with the provided text

| **-t**, **\--trim** [type]
|        Trim the delimiter (greedy).
|        Valid values are (l|L)eft, (r|R)ight, (b|B)oth

|     **\--fallback-oob** [fallback]
|        Generic fallback output for any field that
|        cannot be found (oob stands for out of bound).
|        It's overridden by any fallback assigned to a
|        specific field (see -f for help)

| **-M**, **\--fixed-memory** [size]
|        Read the input in chunks of <size> kilobytes.
|        This allows to read lines arbitrarily large.
|        Works only with single-byte delimiters,
|        fields in ascending order, -z, -j, -r

OPTIONS PRECEDENCE
==================

\--trim and \--compress-delimiter are applied before \--fields or similar

MEMORY CONSUMPTION
==================

\--characters and \--fields read and allocate memory one line at a time

| \--lines allocate memory one line at a time as long as the requested fields are
| ordered and non-negative (e.g. -l 1,3:4,4,7), otherwise it allocates
| the whole input in memory (it also happens when -p or -m are being used)

\--bytes allocate the whole input in memory

| \--fixed-memory will read the input in chunks of <size> kilobytes. This
| allows to read lines arbitrarily large. Works only with single-byte
| delimiters, fields in ascending order, -z, -j, -r

COLORS
======

| Help is displayed using colors. Colors will be suppressed in the
| following circumstances:

- when the TERM environment variable is not set or set to "dumb"
- when the NO_COLOR environment variable is set (regardless of value)

BUGS
====

See GitHub Issues: <https://github.com/riquito/tuc/issues>

AUTHOR
======

Riccardo Attilio Galli <riccardo@sideralis.org>

SEE ALSO
========

**cut(1)**, **sed(1)**, **awk(1)**

tuc 1.3.0
Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts.

USAGE:
    tuc [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] < input
    tuc [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] filepath

FLAGS:
    -g, --greedy-delimiter        Match consecutive delimiters as if it was one
    -p, --compress-delimiter      Print only the first delimiter of a sequence
    -s, --only-delimited          Print only lines containing the delimiter
    -V, --version                 Print version information
    -z, --zero-terminated         Line delimiter is NUL (\0), not LF (\n)
    -h, --help                    Print this help and exit
    -m, --complement              Invert fields (e.g. '2' becomes '1,3:')
    -j, --(no-)join               Print selected parts with delimiter in between
    --json                        Print fields as a JSON array of strings
    --no-mmap                     Disable memory mapping

OPTIONS:
    -f, --fields <bounds>         Fields to keep, 1-indexed, comma separated.
                                  Use colon (:) to match a range (inclusive).
                                  Use equal (=) to apply out of bound fallback.
                                  Fields can be negative (-1 is the last field).
                                  [default: 1:]

                                  e.g. cutting the string 'a-b-c-d' on '-'
                                    -f 1     => a
                                    -f 1:    => a-b-c-d
                                    -f 1:3   => a-b-c
                                    -f 3,2   => cb
                                    -f 3,1:2 => ca-b
                                    -f -3:-2 => b-c
                                    -f 1,8=fallback => afallback

                                  To re-apply the delimiter add -j, to replace
                                  it add -r (followed by the new delimiter).

                                  You can also format the output using {} syntax
                                  e.g.
                                    -f '({1}, {2})' => (a, b)

                                  You can escape { and } using {{ and }}.

    -b, --bytes <bounds>          Same as --fields, but it keeps bytes
    -c, --characters <bounds>     Same as --fields, but it keeps characters
    -l, --lines <bounds>          Same as --fields, but it keeps lines
                                  Implies --join. To merge lines, use --no-join
    -d, --delimiter <delimiter>   Delimiter used by --fields to cut the text
                                  [default: \t]
    -e, --regex <some regex>      Use a regular expression as delimiter
    -r, --replace-delimiter <new> Replace the delimiter with the provided text.
                                  Implies --join
    -t, --trim <type>             Trim the delimiter (greedy). Valid values are
                                  (l|L)eft, (r|R)ight, (b|B)oth
        --fallback-oob <fallback> Generic fallback output for any field that
                                  cannot be found (oob stands for out of bound).
                                  It's overridden by any fallback assigned to a
                                  specific field (see -f for help)
    -M, --fixed-memory <size>     Read the input in chunks of <size> kilobytes.
                                  This allows to read lines arbitrarily large.
                                  Works only with single-byte delimiters,
                                  fields in ascending order, -z, -j, -r

Options precedence:
    --trim and --compress-delimiter are applied before --fields or similar

Memory consumption:
    --characters and --fields read and allocate memory one line at a time

    --lines allocate memory one line at a time as long as the requested fields
    are ordered and non-negative (e.g. -l 1,3:4,4,7), otherwise it allocates
    the whole input in memory (it also happens when -p or -m are being used)

    allows to read lines arbitrarily large. Works only with single-byte

Colors:
    Help is displayed using colors. Colors will be suppressed in the

    - when the NO_COLOR environment variable is set (regardless of value)

{"command":"set -e
# basic
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1:
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1:3
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 3,2
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 3,1:2 -j
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 3,1:2
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f -3:-2
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,8=fallback -j
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,8=fallback
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -r ':'
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f '({1}, {2})'
printf "escaped {{1}} {1}\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 'escaped {{1}} {1}' || true
echo "--- only delimited"
printf "a-b\nc\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1
printf "a-b\nc\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1 -s
echo "--- greedy"
printf "a--b---c\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j
printf "a--b---c\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -g
printf "a--b---c\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -p
echo "--- trim"
printf -- "--a--b--c--\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -t l
printf -- "--a--b--c--\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -t r
printf -- "--a--b--c--\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -t b
printf -- "--a--b--c--\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -t b -g
printf -- "--a--b--c--\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -t left
printf -- "--a--b--c--\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -t right
printf -- "--a--b--c--\n" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -j -t both
echo "--- complement"
echo "a-b-c-d" | ./executable -d '-' -f 2 -m -j
echo "--- join vs no join"
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,2
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,2 -j
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,2 --join
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,2 --no-join
echo "--- lines"
printf "a\nb\nc\nd\ne\n" | ./executable -l 2:-2
printf "a\nb\nc\nd\ne\n" | ./executable -l 2:-2 --no-join
printf "a\nb\nc\nd\ne\n" | ./executable -l 1,3
printf "a\nb\nc\nd\ne\n" | ./executable -l 1,5
printf "a\nb\nc\nd\ne\n" | ./executable -l -2:
echo "--- bytes"
echo "abcde" | ./executable -b 1:3
echo "abcde" | ./executable -b 2,4 -j
echo "abcde" | ./executable -b 2,4
echo "--- characters"
echo "héllo" | ./executable -c 1:3
echo "héllo" | ./executable -c 2 -j  # join irrelevant?
echo "--- json"
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,2 --json
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: --json
echo "--- zero term"
printf "a-b-c\0d-e-f\0" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1 -z | od -c
printf "a-b-c\0d-e-f\0" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1 -z -j | od -c
echo "--- regex"
echo "a1b22c333d" | ./executable -e '[0-9]+' -f 1: -j
echo "a1b22c333d" | ./executable -e '[0-9]+' -f 2 -j
echo "--- fallback"
echo "a-b" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,5 --fallback-oob X -j
echo "a-b" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,5=Z --fallback-oob X -j
echo "--- format"
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f '({1}, {3})'
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f '{2}' -j  # join ignored?
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 'prefix {1:2} suffix' -j
echo "--- replace"
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1: -r ','
echo "a-b-c" | ./executable -d '-' -f 1,3 -r ','
"}

tuc 1.3.0
Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts.

USAGE:
    tuc [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] < input
    tuc [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] filepath

FLAGS:
    -g, --greedy-delimiter        Match consecutive delimiters as if it was one
    -p, --compress-delimiter      Print only the first delimiter of a sequence
    -s, --only-delimited          Print only lines containing the delimiter
    -V, --version                 Print version information
    -z, --zero-terminated         Line delimiter is NUL (\0), not LF (\n)
    -h, --help                    Print this help and exit
    -m, --complement              Invert fields (e.g. '2' becomes '1,3:')
    -j, --(no-)join               Print selected parts with delimiter in between
    --json                        Print fields as a JSON array of strings
    --no-mmap                     Disable memory mapping

OPTIONS:
    -f, --fields <bounds>         Fields to keep, 1-indexed, comma separated.
                                  Use colon (:) to match a range (inclusive).
                                  Use equal (=) to apply out of bound fallback.
                                  Fields can be negative (-1 is the last field).
                                  [default: 1:]

                                  e.g. cutting the string 'a-b-c-d' on '-'
                                    -f 1     => a
                                    -f 1:    => a-b-c-d
                                    -f 1:3   => a-b-c
                                    -f 3,2   => cb
                                    -f 3,1:2 => ca-b
                                    -f -3:-2 => b-c
                                    -f 1,8=fallback => afallback

                                  To re-apply the delimiter add -j, to replace
                                  it add -r (followed by the new delimiter).

                                  You can also format the output using {} syntax
                                  e.g.
                                    -f '({1}, {2})' => (a, b)

                                  You can escape { and } using {{ and }}.

    -b, --bytes <bounds>          Same as --fields, but it keeps bytes
    -c, --characters <bounds>     Same as --fields, but it keeps characters
    -l, --lines <bounds>          Same as --fields, but it keeps lines
                                  Implies --join. To merge lines, use --no-join
    -d, --delimiter <delimiter>   Delimiter used by --fields to cut the text
                                  [default: \t]
    -e, --regex <some regex>      Use a regular expression as delimiter
    -r, --replace-delimiter <new> Replace the delimiter with the provided text.
                                  Implies --join
    -t, --trim <type>             Trim the delimiter (greedy). Valid values are
                                  (l|L)eft, (r|R)ight, (b|B)oth
        --fallback-oob <fallback> Generic fallback output for any field that
                                  cannot be found (oob stands for out of bound).
                                  It's overridden by any fallback assigned to a
                                  specific field (see -f for help)
    -M, --fixed-memory <size>     Read the input in chunks of <size> kilobytes.
                                  This allows to read lines arbitrarily large.
                                  Works only with single-byte delimiters,
                                  fields in ascending order, -z, -j, -r

Options precedence:
    --trim and --compress-delimiter are applied before --fields or similar

Memory consumption:
    --characters and --fields read and allocate memory one line at a time

    the whole input in memory (it also happens when -p or -m are being used)

    --bytes allocate the whole input in memory

tuc 1.3.0 - Created by Riccardo Attilio Galli

Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts.

# tuc

Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts.

Install
-------
Download one of the prebuilt binaries from the releases page for your platform, or use a system package if available.

Try it out online
-----------------
Play with a webassembly version online: https://riquito.github.io/tuc/playground/index.html

Demo
----

![demo](./doc/screencast.svg)

Usage (short)
-------------

	Usage: tuc [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] < input
	       tuc [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] filepath

Flags and options, examples and full documentation are available in the man page (doc/tuc.1) and the examples below.

Examples
--------

# Cut and rearrange fields
echo "foo bar baz" | tuc -d ' ' -f 3,2,1

# Join fields back with the delimiter
echo "foo bar baz" | tuc -d ' ' -f 3,2,1 -j

# Cut lines (keep everything between first and last line)
printf "a\nb\nc\nd\ne" | tuc -l 2:-2

For more examples and full option reference, see doc/tuc.1 and doc/tuc.1.md.
</output>

#!/bin/bash
set +e
bin=./executable
# We need to understand greedy vs compress semantics thoroughly.

# Definitions from docs:
# -g --greedy-delimiter: Match consecutive delimiters as if it was one
# -p --compress-delimiter: Print only the first delimiter of a sequence

# But earlier tests show:
# Input "a::b::c", delimiter ":", fields 1: -j
# - no flag: a::b::c  (join with : prints delimiters as originally? Actually join should re-insert delimiter between fields. For 1: which is all fields, join should reconstruct original? It does a::b::c)
# - with -g: a::b::c (same)
# - with -p: a:b:c (compresses consecutive delimiters when printing to one)

# What about fields 1:2?
# a::b::c splitted:
# Without g/p: fields = ["a","","b","","c"] (5 fields)
# 1:2 => ["a",""] -> join with ":" => "a:" (since delimiter between them is ":")
# With -g: fields = ["a","b","c"] (greedy collapses consecutive delimiters during splitting)
# 1:2 with -g => ["a","b"] -> join => "a::b"? Wait earlier we saw a::b for -g, not a:b. Let's see.
# If delimiter is ":", greedy meaning consecutive delimiters match as one, so split would treat "::" as one delimiter, but when joining with -j, does it preserve original delimiter sequence or use single delimiter?
# Observations:
# Input "a::b::c", -f 1:2 -j:
# no flag => a:
# -g => a::b
# -p => a:b

# So for 1:2 -j:
# no flag: fields a and "" joined with ":" => "a:" (matches our expectation: first delimiter is ":")
# -g: fields a,b joined but original delimiters between a and b was "::" (two colons) collapsed as one delimiter? Yet output was "a::b" (two colons) not "a:b". So greedy does NOT compress the delimiter sequence in output when using -j? Wait but -g gave a::b meaning it kept the original delimiter sequence "::" when joining? That seems contrary to "match consecutive as if it was one" => should be one delimiter, but output shows "::" preserved.

# Let's test -g vs -p difference for 1:2:
# -g gave a::b (keeps ::)
# -p gave a:b (compresses :: to :)

# For full range 1: -j:
# no flag => a::b::c (original)
# -g => a::b::c (same)
# -p => a:b:c (compressed)

# So both -g and -p result in same for full range? Actually for full range, -g also gave a::b::c, not compressed. Wait earlier we saw -g gave a::b::c for full range, same as no flag. So -g did not compress full range output, while -p did.

# Let's test more: input "a::b::c", -f 1:3 -j:
# no flag => a::b (since fields 1,2,3 = a, "", b => join with ":"? Actually fields 1: a, 2:"", 3:b. Joining: a + ":" + "" + ":" + b = "a::b" . That matches earlier: we saw for 1:3 no flag gave "a::b" (yes)
# -g => a::b::c? Wait 1:3 with -g should be fields a,b,c => join => "a::b::c"? But we saw earlier for 1:3 with -g gave "a::b::c" (yes)
# -p => a:b:c

# So pattern: -p compresses delimiter sequences when joining, -g does NOT compress when joining, but does affect splitting (collapsing empty fields).

# Let's test fields with -g and -p JSON (which shows fields, not joined output):
# a::b::c, f 1: --json
# no flag => ["a","","b","","c"]
# -g => ["a","b","c"] (empty fields removed)
# -p => ["a","b","c"] (same as -g for JSON? Actually compress also collapses empty fields for counting? For JSON, -p gave ["a","b","c"] as well.)

# What about -j vs no -j for fields with empty?
# Input "a::b::c", -f 1,3 (no join) => should be "ab" (concatenation without delimiter). Let's check:
echo "a::b::c" | ./executable -d ":" -f 1,3
echo "a::b::c" | ./executable -d ":" -f 1,3 -j
echo "a::b::c" | ./executable -d ":" -f 1,3 -g
echo "a::b::c" | ./executable -d ":" -f 1,3 -g -j
echo "a::b::c" | ./executable -d ":" -f 1,3 -p
echo "a::b::c" | ./executable -d ":" -f 1,3 -p -j

# For 1,3 no join vs join:
# no flag: fields a and b? Actually field 3 is "b" (since fields: 1:a,2:"",3:b). So concatenation => "ab"
# -j => "a:b" (join with delimiter)
# With -g: fields 1:a,3:c (since after greedy collapse, fields become a,b,c). So 1,3 => a,c => concatenation "ac", join "a:c"
# With -p: fields 1:a,3:c as well? Since after compress? Let's test:
echo "a::b::c" | ./executable -d ":" -f 1,3 --json -p
echo "a::b::c" | ./executable -d ":" -f 1,3 --json -g

# So -p also collapses empty fields for field counting, same as -g for JSON.
# But difference between -g and -p appears in join output when range includes consecutive delimiters: 
# For -g, join preserves original delimiter sequence? For -p, join compresses to single delimiter.
# Example: input "a::b::c", -f 1:2 -j -g gave "a::b" (preserves ::)
# While -f 1:2 -j -p gave "a:b" (compresses :: to :)

# For full range 1: -j -g gave "a::b::c" (preserves), -p gave "a:b:c" (compresses)

# So summary:
# -g (greedy delimiter) affects splitting: consecutive delimiters are treated as one separator, so empty fields between them are discarded. But when re-joining with -j, it uses the original delimiter material? Actually "a::b" output for 1:2 -g suggests that the delimiter between a and b was "::" (two colons) preserved, even though splitting treated "::" as one. So join uses original delimiter occurrence? Hmm.

# -p (compress delimiter) affects both splitting and printing: consecutive delimiters are collapsed to one for field counting (like -g) AND when printing with join, only first delimiter of sequence is printed.

# Wait doc: -p "Print only the first delimiter of a sequence"
# -g "Match consecutive delimiters as if it was one"
# So both affect field counting similarly for splitting (both collapse empties), but difference is in printing:
# -g when printing with join, should still print the whole delimiter sequence? Or maybe print as originally matched (greedy match = consecutive delimiters). For "a::b", greedy match would be "::" as one delimiter, so when joining, should print "::"? That matches -g output "a::b" for 1:2 (delimiter "::" printed once). While -p output "a:b" prints only first ":" of sequence.

# Let's test multi-char delimiter "--" with input "a----b" (which is "--"+"--")
# Delimiter "--"
# Input "a----b" -> splitting:
# Without flags: delimiter "--" occurs at pos 2-3 and 4-5? Actually string "a----b" = a + -- + -- + b . That's two delimiters "--" consecutively, with empty field between? Let's see fields:
# a----b with -- delimiter:
# Should be ["a","","b"]? Let's check JSON:
echo "a----b" | ./executable -d "--" -f 1: --json
echo "a----b" | ./executable -d "--" -f 1: --json -g
echo "a----b" | ./executable -d "--" -f 1: --json -p

# Results: earlier we saw:
# no flag => ["a","","b"]? Let's verify with earlier data: we had a--b----c but not a----b. Let's test now.

EOS
chmod +x /tmp/understand_greedy.sh
/tmp/understand_greedy.sh 2>&1

# With -j => join with delimiter

echo "a:b:c" | $bin -d ":" -f 1,2 -r "," | cat -A # a,b

# For lines

% tuc(1) Tuc 1.3.0 | Tuc Manual
%
% Sep 10, 2025

NAME
====

**tuc** — cut text or bytes and keep what you need

SYNOPSIS
========

| **tuc** \[FLAGS]... \[OPTIONS]... \< input
| **tuc** \[FLAGS]... \[OPTIONS]... filepath

DESCRIPTION
===========

Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts.  

FLAGS
=====

-g, \--greedy-delimiter
:   Match consecutive delimiters as if it was one

-p, \--compress-delimiter
:   Print only the first delimiter of a sequence

-s, \--only-delimited
:   Print only lines containing the delimiter

-V, \--version
:   Print version information

-z, \--zero-terminated
:   Line delimiter is NUL (\0), not LF (\\n)

-h, \--help
:   Print this help and exit

-m, \--complement
:   Invert fields (e.g. \'2\' becomes \'1,3:\')

-j, \--(no-)join
:   Print selected parts with delimiter in between

\--json
:   Print fields as a JSON array of strings

\--no-mmap
:   Disable memory mapping

OPTIONS
=======

| **-f**, **\--fields** [bounds]
|        Fields to keep, 1-indexed, comma separated.
|        Use colon (:) to match a range (inclusive).
|        Use equal (=) to apply out of bound fallback.
|        Fields can be negative (-1 is the last field).

|        [default 1:]

|        e.g. cutting the string \'a-b-c-d\' on \'-\'
|          `-f 1     => a`
|          `-f 1:    => a-b-c-d`
|          `-f 1:3   => a-b-c`
|          `-f 3,2   => cb`
|          `-f 3,1:2 => ca-b`
|          `-f -3:-2 => b-c`
|          `-f 1,8=fallback => afallback`

|        To re-apply the delimiter add -j, to replace
|        it add -r (followed by the new delimiter)

|        You can also format the output using {} syntax
|        e.g.
|          `-f '({1}, {2})' => (a, b)`

|        You can escape { and } using {{ and }}.

| **-b**, **\--bytes** [bounds]
|        Same as \--fields, but it keeps bytes

| **-c**, **\--characters** [bounds]
|        Same as \--fields, but it keeps characters

| **-l**, **\--lines** [bounds]
|        Same as \--fields, but it keeps lines
|        Implies \--join. To merge lines, use \--no-join

| **-d**, **\--delimiter** [delimiter]
|        Delimiter used by \--fields to cut the text
|        [default: \\t]

| **-e**, **\--regex** [some regex]
|        Use a regular expression as delimiter

| **-r**, **\--replace-delimiter** [new delimiter]
</output>

tuc 1.3.0
Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts.

USAGE:
    tuc [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] < input
    tuc [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] filepath

FLAGS:
    -g, --greedy-delimiter        Match consecutive delimiters as if it was one
    -p, --compress-delimiter      Print only the first delimiter of a sequence
    -s, --only-delimited          Print only lines containing the delimiter
    -V, --version                 Print version information
    -z, --zero-terminated         Line delimiter is NUL (\0), not LF (\n)
    -h, --help                    Print this help and exit
    -m, --complement              Invert fields (e.g. '2' becomes '1,3:')
    -j, --(no-)join               Print selected parts with delimiter in between
    --json                        Print fields as a JSON array of strings
    --no-mmap                     Disable memory mapping

OPTIONS:
    -f, --fields <bounds>         Fields to keep, 1-indexed, comma separated.
                                  Use colon (:) to match a range (inclusive).
                                  Use equal (=) to apply out of bound fallback.
                                  Fields can be negative (-1 is the last field).
                                  [default: 1:]

                                  e.g. cutting the string 'a-b-c-d' on '-'
                                    -f 1     => a
                                    -f 1:    => a-b-c-d
                                    -f 1:3   => a-b-c
                                    -f 3,2   => cb
                                    -f 3,1:2 => ca-b
                                    -f -3:-2 => b-c
                                    -f 1,8=fallback => afallback

                                  To re-apply the delimiter add -j, to replace
                                  it add -r (followed by the new delimiter).

                                  You can also format the output using {} syntax
                                  e.g.
                                    -f '({1}, {2})' => (a, b)

                                  You can escape { and } using {{ and }}.

    -b, --bytes <bounds>          Same as --fields, but it keeps bytes
    -c, --characters <bounds>     Same as --fields, but it keeps characters
    -l, --lines <bounds>          Same as --fields, but it keeps lines
                                  Implies --join. To merge lines, use --no-join
    -d, --delimiter <delimiter>   Delimiter used by --fields to cut the text
                                  [default: \t]
    -e, --regex <some regex>      Use a regular expression as delimiter
    -r, --replace-delimiter <new> Replace the delimiter with the provided text.
                                  Implies --join
    -t, --trim <type>             Trim the delimiter (greedy). Valid values are
                                  (l|L)eft, (r|R)ight, (b|B)oth
        --fallback-oob <fallback> Generic fallback output for any field that
                                  cannot be found (oob stands for out of bound).
                                  It's overridden by any fallback assigned to a
                                  specific field (see -f for help)
    -M, --fixed-memory <size>     Read the input in chunks of <size> kilobytes.
                                  This allows to read lines arbitrarily large.
                                  Works only with single-byte delimiters,
                                  fields in ascending order, -z, -j, -r

Options precedence:
    --trim and --compress-delimiter are applied before --fields or similar

Memory consumption:
    --characters and --fields read and allocate memory one line at a time

    --lines allocate memory one line at a time as long as the requested fields
    are ordered and non-negative (e.g. -l 1,3:4,4,7), otherwise it allocates
    the whole input in memory (it also happens when -p or -m are being used)

    --bytes allocate the whole input in memory

Colors:

tuc 1.3.0 - Created by Riccardo Attilio Galli

Cut text (or bytes) where a delimiter matches, then keep the desired parts.

Some examples:

# Bounds parsing

class BoundItem:
    def __init__(self, kind, left=None, right=None, value=None, fallback=None, raw=None):

        self.left = left
        self.right = right
        self.value = value
        self.fallback = fallback
        self.raw = raw

def parse_trim_type(s):
    if s in ('l','L'): return 'left'
    if s in ('r','R'): return 'right'
    if s in ('b','B'): return 'both'
    raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{s}': Valid trim values are (l|L)eft, (r|R)ight, (b|B)oth")

def parse_single_token(token, full):
    # split fallback
    if '=' in token:
        idx = token.find('=')
        main_part = token[:idx]
        fallback = token[idx+1:]
    else:
        main_part = token
        fallback = None

        right_s = main_part[colon+1:]
        if left_s=='' and right_s=='':
            raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Field format error, no numbers next to `:`")
        left_opt = None
        right_opt = None
        if left_s!='':
            try:
                v=int(left_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Not a number `{left_s}`")
            if v==0:
                raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Zero is not a valid field")
            left_opt=v
        if right_s!='':
            try:
                v=int(right_s)
            except:
                raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Not a number `{right_s}`")
            if v==0:
                raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Zero is not a valid field")
            right_opt=v
        if left_opt is not None and right_opt is not None:
            if left_opt>0 and right_opt>0 and left_opt>right_opt:
                raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Field left value cannot be greater than right value")
            if left_opt<0 and right_opt<0 and left_opt>right_opt:
                raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Field left value cannot be greater than right value")
        return BoundItem(kind='range', left=left_opt, right=right_opt, fallback=fallback, raw=token)
    else:
        try:
            v=int(main_part)
        except:
            raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Not a number `{main_part}`")
        if v==0:
            raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Zero is not a valid field")
        return BoundItem(kind='single', value=v, fallback=fallback, raw=token)

def parse_bounds_list(full):
    if full=='':
        raise ValueError("failed to parse '': Field format error: empty field")
    if any(p=='' for p in full.split(',')):
        raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{full}': Field format error: empty field")
    res=[]
    for part in full.split(','):
        # check brace errors? We'll handle in is_format detection before calling
        res.append(parse_single_token(part, full))
    if len(res)==0:
        raise RuntimeError("UserBoundsList must contain at least one UserBounds")
    return res

def parse_bounds_list_with_outer(inner, outer):
    if inner=='':
        raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{outer}': Field format error: empty field")
    if any(p=='' for p in inner.split(',')):
        raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{outer}': Field format error: empty field")
    res=[]
    for part in inner.split(','):
        res.append(parse_single_token(part, outer))
    return res

def is_format_string(s):
    return '{' in s or '}' in s

def parse_format(s):
    chars = list(s)
    i=0
    parts=[]
    lit=''
    has_ph=False
    while i < len(chars):
        ch=chars[i]
        if ch=='{':
            if i+1 < len(chars) and chars[i+1]=='{':
                lit+='{'
                i+=2
            else:
                if lit!='':
                    parts.append(('lit', lit))
                    lit=''
                # find next '}'
                j=i+1
                close=None
                while j < len(chars):
                    if chars[j]=='}':
                        close=j
                        break
                    j+=1
                if close is None:
                    raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{s}': Field format error: missing closing parenthesis")
                content=''.join(chars[i+1:close])
                if content=='':
                    raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{s}': Field format error: empty field")
                bounds = parse_bounds_list_with_outer(content, s)
                has_ph=True
                parts.append(('ph', bounds))
                i=close+1
        elif ch=='}':
            if i+1 < len(chars) and chars[i+1]=='}':
                lit+='}'
                i+=2
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"failed to parse '{s}': Field format error: missing opening parenthesis")
        else:
            lit+=ch
            i+=1
    if lit!='':
        parts.append(('lit', lit))
    if not has_ph:
        raise RuntimeError("UserBoundsList must contain at least one UserBounds")
    return parts

def json_escape_py(s):
    # match original json escaping: use json module?
    # json module escapes differently? We'll implement manual similar to rust's serde_json?
    # For simplicity use json.dumps then strip quotes? json.dumps adds escapes for quotes, backslash, and control chars as \n etc.
    # Let's use json.dumps(s) which returns quoted string, we want inner escaped content plus handling?
    # We'll use our manual from earlier: escape ",\, \b,\f,\n,\r,\t and control as \uXXXX
    out=''
    for c in s:
        if c=='"':
            out+='\\"'
        elif c=='\\':
            out+='\\\\'
        elif c=='\b':
            out+='\\b'
        elif c=='\f':
            out+='\\f'
        elif c=='\n':
            out+='\\n'
        elif c=='\r':
            out+='\\r'
        elif c=='\t':
            out+='\\t'
        elif ord(c) < 0x20:
            out+=f'\\u{ord(c):04x}'
        else:
            out+=c
    return out

def split_fields_by_str(line, pattern, greedy):
    if pattern=='':
        return {'fields':[line], 'delims':[], 'counts':[]}
    # find occurrences non-overlapping
    occ=[]
    search=0
    while search <= len(line):
        idx = line.find(pattern, search)
        if idx==-1:
            break
        occ.append((idx, idx+len(pattern)))
        search = idx+len(pattern)
    if not occ:
        return {'fields':[line], 'delims':[], 'counts':[]}
    if greedy:
        grouped=[]
        i=0
        while i < len(occ):
            rs, re = occ[i]
            cnt=1
            j=i+1
            while j < len(occ) and occ[j][0]==re:
                re=occ[j][1]
                cnt+=1
                j+=1
            grouped.append((rs,re,cnt))
            i=j
        fields=[]
        delims=[]
        counts=[]
        last=0
        for rs,re,cnt in grouped:
            fields.append(line[last:rs])
            delims.append(line[rs:re])
            counts.append(cnt)
            last=re
        fields.append(line[last:])
        return {'fields':fields, 'delims':delims, 'counts':counts}
    else:
        fields=[]
        delims=[]
        counts=[]
        last=0
        for s,e in occ:
            fields.append(line[last:s])
            delims.append(pattern)
            counts.append(1)
            last=e
        fields.append(line[last:])
        return {'fields':fields, 'delims':delims, 'counts':counts}

def split_fields_by_regex(line, regex, greedy):
    matches = list(regex.finditer(line))
    if not matches:
        return {'fields':[line], 'delims':[], 'counts':[]}
    if greedy:
        grouped=[]
        i=0
        while i < len(matches):
            rs = matches[i].start()
            re_end = matches[i].end()
            cnt=1
            j=i+1
            while j < len(matches) and matches[j].start()==re_end:
                re_end = matches[j].end()
                cnt+=1
                j+=1
            grouped.append((rs,re_end,cnt))
            i=j
        fields=[]
        delims=[]
        counts=[]
        last=0
        for rs,re,cnt in grouped:
            fields.append(line[last:rs])
            delims.append(line[rs:re])
            counts.append(cnt)
            last=re
        fields.append(line[last:])
        return {'fields':fields, 'delims':delims, 'counts':counts}
    else:
        fields=[]
        delims=[]
        counts=[]
        last=0
        for m in matches:
            fields.append(line[last:m.start()])
            delims.append(m.group())
            counts.append(1)
            last=m.end()
        fields.append(line[last:])
        return {'fields':fields, 'delims':delims, 'counts':counts}

def trim_line(line, delim_info, trim_type):
    if delim_info['is_regex']:
        re = delim_info['regex']
        s=line
        if trim_type in ('left','both'):
            while True:
                m=re.search(s)
                if m and m.start()==0:
                    s=s[m.end():]
                else:
                    break
        if trim_type in ('right','both'):
            while True:
                # find match ending at end
                found=None
                for mm in re.finditer(s):
                    if mm.end()==len(s):
                        found=mm
                if found:
                    s=s[:found.start()]
                else:
                    break
        return s
    else:
        pat=delim_info['pattern']
        if pat=='':
            return line
        s=line
        if trim_type in ('left','both'):
            while s.startswith(pat):
                s=s[len(pat):]
        if trim_type in ('right','both'):
            while s.endswith(pat):
                s=s[:len(s)-len(pat)]
        return s

def compress_line_fn(line, delim_info):
    if delim_info['is_regex']:
        re=delim_info['regex']
        result=''
        last=0
        matches=list(re.finditer(line))
        i=0
        while i < len(matches):
            rs=matches[i].start()
            re_end=matches[i].end()
            j=i+1
            while j < len(matches) and matches[j].start()==re_end:
                re_end=matches[j].end()
                j+=1
            result+=line[last:rs]
            result+=matches[i].group()
            last=re_end
            i=j
        result+=line[last:]
        return result
    else:
        pat=delim_info['pattern']
        if pat=='':
            return line
        occ=[]
        search=0
        while search <= len(line):
            idx=line.find(pat, search)
            if idx==-1:
                break
            occ.append((idx, idx+len(pat)))
            search=idx+len(pat)
        if not occ:
            return line
        grouped=[]
        i=0
        while i < len(occ):
            rs,re=occ[i]
            j=i+1
            while j < len(occ) and occ[j][0]==re:
                re=occ[j][1]
                j+=1
            grouped.append((rs,re))
            i=j
        res=''
        last=0
        for s,e in grouped:
            res+=line[last:s]
            res+=pat
            last=e
        res+=line[last:]
        return res

def build_range_slice(split, start, end, replace):
    # start,end 1-indexed
    if start==0 or end==0 or start>len(split['fields']) or end>len(split['fields']) or start>end:
        return ''
    s=''
    for idx in range(start, end+1):
        s+=split['fields'][idx-1]
        if idx != end:
            delim_idx = idx-1
            if delim_idx < len(split['delims']):
                cnt = split['counts'][delim_idx]
                orig = split['delims'][delim_idx]
                if replace is not None:
                    s+=replace* cnt
                else:
                    s+=orig
    return s

def resolve_bounds_list(fields_len, bounds, fallback_oob):
    out=[]
    for b in bounds:
        if b.kind=='single':
            v=b.value
            if v>0:
                pos = v if v<=fields_len else None
            else:
                p = fields_len + v +1
                pos = p if 1 <= p <= fields_len else None
            if pos is None:
                fb = b.fallback if b.fallback is not None else fallback_oob
                if fb is not None:
                    out.append({'start':0, 'end':0, 'fallback':fb, 'raw':b.raw, 'is_range':False})
                else:
                    raise IndexError(f"Error: Out of bounds: {b.raw}")
            else:
                out.append({'start':pos, 'end':pos, 'fallback':b.fallback, 'raw':b.raw, 'is_range':False})
        else: # range
            left_val = b.left if b.left is not None else 1
            right_val = b.right if b.right is not None else fields_len

            # left pos
            if b.left is None:
                left_pos=1
            else:
                lv=left_val
                if lv>0:
                    if lv>fields_len:
                        left_pos=None
                    else:
                        left_pos=lv
                else:
                    p=fields_len+lv+1
                    if p<1:
                        left_pos=None
                    else:
                        left_pos=p
            # right pos with clamping for fields
            if b.right is None:
                right_pos=fields_len
            else:
                rv=right_val
                if rv>0:
                    if rv>fields_len:
                        right_pos=fields_len
                    else:
                        right_pos=rv
                else:
                    p=fields_len+rv+1
                    if p<1:
                        right_pos=1
                    else:
                        right_pos=p

            if left_pos is None:
                fb = b.fallback if b.fallback is not None else fallback_oob
                if fb is not None:
                    out.append({'start':0, 'end':0, 'fallback':fb, 'raw':b.raw, 'is_range':True})
                    continue
                else:
                    raise IndexError(f"Error: Out of bounds: {left_val}")

            if left_pos > right_pos:
                fb = b.fallback if b.fallback is not None else fallback_oob
                if fb is not None:
                    out.append({'start':0, 'end':0, 'fallback':fb, 'raw':b.raw, 'is_range':True})
                    continue
                else:
                    raise ValueError("Error: Field left value cannot be greater than right value")

            out.append({'start':left_pos, 'end':right_pos, 'fallback':b.fallback, 'raw':b.raw, 'is_range':True})
    return out

                if not comp_res:
                    return None, "Error: the complement is empty"
                resolved = comp_res

            pieces=[]
            for res in resolved:
                if res['start']==0:
                    pieces.append(res['fallback'])
                elif res['is_range']:
                    pieces.append(build_range_slice(split, res['start'], res['end'], replace))
                else:
                    pieces.append(split['fields'][res['start']-1])
            # placeholder internal join
            if join_flag==True or replace is not None:
                jd = replace if replace is not None else ('' if delim_info['is_regex'] else delim_info['pattern'])
                ph_str = jd.join(pieces)
            else:
                ph_str = ''.join(pieces)
            ph_exps.append(ph_str)

    # outer join logic
    ph_positions = [i for i, p in enumerate(format_parts) if p[0]=='ph']
    final_out=''
    ph_idx=0
    last_was_ph=False
    for idx, part in enumerate(format_parts):
        if part[0]=='lit':
            l=part[1]
            is_between = False
            # find prev ph < idx and next ph > idx
            prev_ph = None
            for pos in ph_positions:
                if pos < idx:
                    prev_ph = pos
                else:
                    break
            next_ph = None
            for pos in ph_positions:
                if pos > idx:
                    next_ph = pos
                    break
            if prev_ph is not None and next_ph is not None:
                is_between=True
            if join_flag==True and is_between:
                jd = replace if replace is not None else ('' if delim_info['is_regex'] else delim_info['pattern'])
                final_out+=jd
                final_out+=l
            else:
                final_out+=l
            last_was_ph=False
        else: # ph
            if last_was_ph and join_flag==True:
                jd = replace if replace is not None else ('' if delim_info['is_regex'] else delim_info['pattern'])
                final_out+=jd
            final_out+=ph_exps[ph_idx]
            ph_idx+=1
            last_was_ph=True

    return final_out, None

def main():
    args = sys.argv

    if len(args)==1:
        # short help
        sys.stdout.write(short_help())
        sys.exit(0)

    # early version/help
    for a in args[1:]:
        if a in ('-V','--version'):
            sys.stdout.write(f"tuc {VERSION}\n")
            sys.exit(0)
        if a in ('-h','--help'):
            sys.stdout.write(long_help())
            sys.exit(0)

    # parse
    greedy=False
    compress=False
    only_delimited=False
    zero_terminated=False
    complement=False
    join_flag=None
    json_flag=False
    no_mmap=False

    fields_opt=None
    bytes_opt=None
    chars_opt=None
    lines_opt=None
    delimiter_opt=None
    regex_opt=None
    replace_opt=None
    trim_opt=None
    fallback_oob_opt=None
    fixed_memory_opt=None
    filepath=None

    i=1
    while i < len(args):
        arg=args[i]
        # combined pure flags
        if arg.startswith('-') and not arg.startswith('--') and len(arg)>2:
            first = arg[1]
            if first in 'fbcldertM':
                # attached value
                opt_char=first
                attached=arg[2:]
                if attached.startswith('='):
                    attached=attached[1:]
                def get_val(att):
                    nonlocal i
                    if att=='':
                        if i+1 >= len(args):
                            # missing value
                            name = {'f':'-f','b':'-b','c':'-c','l':'-l','d':'-d','e':'-e','r':'-r','t':'-t','M':'-M'}[opt_char]
                            sys.stderr.write(f"the '{name}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                            sys.exit(1)
                        v=args[i+1]
                        i+=1
                        return v
                    else:
                        return att
                val=get_val(attached)
                if opt_char=='f':
                    if fields_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-f\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    fields_opt=val
                elif opt_char=='b':
                    if bytes_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-b\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    bytes_opt=val
                elif opt_char=='c':
                    if chars_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-c\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    chars_opt=val
                elif opt_char=='l':
                    if lines_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-l\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    lines_opt=val
                elif opt_char=='d':
                    if delimiter_opt is not None or regex_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-d\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    delimiter_opt=val
                elif opt_char=='e':
                    if delimiter_opt is not None or regex_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-e\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    regex_opt=val
                elif opt_char=='r':
                    if replace_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-r\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    replace_opt=val
                elif opt_char=='t':
                    if trim_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-t\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    trim_opt=val
                elif opt_char=='M':
                    if fixed_memory_opt is not None:
                        sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-M\", \"{val}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                        sys.exit(1)
                    fixed_memory_opt=val
                i+=1
                continue
            else:
                # check if all chars in gpszmj
                flag_chars=arg[1:]
                if all(c in 'gpszmj' for c in flag_chars):
                    for ch in flag_chars:
                        if ch=='g':
                            if greedy:
                                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-g\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                                sys.exit(1)
                            greedy=True
                        elif ch=='p':
                            if compress:
                                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-p\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                                sys.exit(1)
                            compress=True
                        elif ch=='s':
                            if only_delimited:
                                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-s\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                                sys.exit(1)
                            only_delimited=True
                        elif ch=='z':
                            if zero_terminated:
                                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-z\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                                sys.exit(1)
                            zero_terminated=True
                        elif ch=='m':
                            if complement:
                                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-m\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                                sys.exit(1)
                            complement=True
                        elif ch=='j':
                            if join_flag is not None:
                                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"-j\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                                sys.exit(1)
                            join_flag=True
                    i+=1
                    continue

        if arg in ('-g','--greedy-delimiter'):
            if greedy:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            greedy=True
        elif arg in ('-p','--compress-delimiter'):
            if compress:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            compress=True
        elif arg in ('-s','--only-delimited'):
            if only_delimited:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            only_delimited=True
        elif arg in ('-z','--zero-terminated'):
            if zero_terminated:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            zero_terminated=True
        elif arg in ('-m','--complement'):
            if complement:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            complement=True
        elif arg in ('-j','--join'):
            if join_flag is not None:
                if join_flag==True:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: runtime error. It's not possible to use --join and --no-join simultaneously\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
            join_flag=True
        elif arg == '--no-join':
            if join_flag is not None:
                if join_flag==False:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
                else:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: runtime error. It's not possible to use --join and --no-join simultaneously\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
            join_flag=False
        elif arg == '--json':
            if json_flag:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            json_flag=True
        elif arg == '--no-mmap':
            if no_mmap:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            no_mmap=True
        elif arg in ('-f','--fields'):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if fields_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            fields_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg in ('-b','--bytes'):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if bytes_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            bytes_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg in ('-c','--characters'):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if chars_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            chars_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg in ('-l','--lines'):
            if i+1>=args.len():
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if lines_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            lines_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg in ('-d','--delimiter'):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if delimiter_opt is not None or regex_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            delimiter_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg in ('-e','--regex'):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if delimiter_opt is not None or regex_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            regex_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg in ('-r','--replace-delimiter'):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if replace_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            replace_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg in ('-t','--trim'):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if trim_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            trim_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg=='--fallback-oob':
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if fallback_oob_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            fallback_oob_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        elif arg in ('-M','--fixed-memory'):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                sys.stderr.write(f"the '{arg}' option doesn't have an associated value\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            if fixed_memory_opt is not None:
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\", \"{args[i+1]}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            fixed_memory_opt=args[i+1]
            i+=1
        else:
            if arg.startswith('-'):
                sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                sys.exit(1)
            else:
                if filepath is not None:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: unexpected arguments: [\"{filepath}\", \"{arg}\"]\nTry 'tuc --help' for more information.\n")
                    sys.exit(1)
                filepath=arg
        i+=1

    # mode
    mode='fields'
    bounds_str=None
    if fields_opt is not None:
        mode='fields'
        bounds_str=fields_opt
    elif bytes_opt is not None:
        mode='bytes'
        bounds_str=bytes_opt
    elif chars_opt is not None:
        mode='chars'
        bounds_str=chars_opt
    elif lines_opt is not None:
        mode='lines'
        bounds_str=lines_opt
    else:
        mode='fields'
        bounds_str='1:'

    # delim_info
    delim_info={}
    if regex_opt is not None:
        try:
            regex = re.compile(regex_opt)
        except re.error as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"regex error: {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        delim_info={'is_regex':True, 'pattern':regex_opt, 'regex':regex}
    else:
        pat = delimiter_opt if delimiter_opt is not None else '\t'
        delim_info={'is_regex':False, 'pattern':pat, 'regex':None}

    # trim type
    trim_type=None
    if trim_opt is not None:
        try:
            tt = parse_trim_type(trim_opt)
        except ValueError as e:
            sys.stderr.write(str(e)+"\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        trim_type=tt

    # join checks
    if mode=='chars':
        if join_flag==False:
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. Since --characters implies --join, you can't pass --no-join\n")
            sys.exit(1)
    if mode=='lines':
        if join_flag is None:
            join_flag=True
    if join_flag==False:
        if replace_opt is not None:
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. You can't pass --no-join when using --replace, which implies --join\n")
            sys.exit(1)

    if delim_info['is_regex']:
        if join_flag==True and replace_opt is None:
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. Cannot use --regex and --join without --replace-delimiter\n")
            sys.exit(1)

    if json_flag:
        if mode in ('bytes','lines'):
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. --json support is available only for --fields and --characters\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        if replace_opt is not None:
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. The use of --replace with --json is not supported\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        if join_flag==False:
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. Using both --json and --no-join is not permitted\n")
            sys.exit(1)

    if compress:
        if mode in ('bytes','chars'):
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. Delimiters can be compressed only with --fields and --lines\n")
            sys.exit(1)

    if fixed_memory_opt is not None:
        if not delim_info['is_regex'] and len(delim_info['pattern'])!=1:
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. Delimiter must be 1 byte wide for FastOpt\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        if greedy or compress or only_delimited or trim_type is not None or complement or json_flag or mode!='fields':
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. StreamOpt supports solely forward fields, join and single-character delimiters\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        if join_flag==False:
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. It's not possible to use --join and --no-join simultaneously\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        if is_format_string(bounds_str):
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. StreamOpt supports solely forward fields, join and single-character delimiters\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        try:
            parsed = parse_bounds_list(bounds_str)
        except ValueError as e:
            sys.stderr.write(str(e)+"\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        except RuntimeError as e:
            sys.stderr.write(str(e)+"\n")
            sys.exit(1)
        # forward check
        prev_end=None
        forward=True
        for item in parsed:
            if item.kind=='single':
                v=item.value
                if v<0:
                    forward=False
                    break
                if prev_end is not None and v <= prev_end:
                    forward=False
                    break
                prev_end=v
            else: # range
                lv = item.left if item.left is not None else 1
                rv = item.right if item.right is not None else 10**18
                if lv<0 or (item.right is not None and rv<0):
                    forward=False
                    break
                if prev_end is not None and lv <= prev_end:
                    forward=False
                    break
                if item.right is not None:
                    prev_end=rv
                else:
                    prev_end=10**18
        # check open ended not last
        for idx, item in enumerate(parsed):
            if item.kind=='range' and item.right is None:
                if idx != len(parsed)-1:
                    forward=False
                    break
        if not forward:
            sys.stderr.write("tuc: runtime error. Bounds cannot be converted to ForwardBounds\n")
            sys.exit(1)

    # read input
    if filepath is not None:
        try:
            with open(filepath, 'rb') as f:
                input_bytes = f.read()
        except Exception as e:
            sys.stderr.write(f"tuc: cannot open file {filepath}: {e}\n")
            sys.exit(1)
    else:
        input_bytes = sys.stdin.buffer.read()

    line_delim = 0 if zero_terminated else 10 # \n

    # Fixed memory
    if fixed_memory_opt is not None:
        data_str = input_bytes.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
        if zero_terminated:
            lines = data_str.split('\0')
        else:
            lines = data_str.split('\n')
        bounds = parse_bounds_list(bounds_str)
        for line_idx, line in enumerate(lines):
            is_last = line_idx == len(lines)-1
            is_trailing = False
            if not zero_terminated:
                if is_last and line=='' and input_bytes.endswith(b'\n'):
                    is_trailing=True
            else:
                if is_last and line=='' and input_bytes.endswith(b'\x00'):
                    is_trailing=True
            if is_trailing:
                continue
            split = split_fields_by_str(line, delim_info['pattern'], False) if not delim_info['is_regex'] else split_fields_by_regex(line, delim_info['regex'], False)
            resolved=[]
            err_msg=None
            for item in bounds:
                if item.kind=='single':
                    v=item.value
                    pos = v if v>0 and v<=len(split['fields']) else None
                    if pos is None:
                        fb = item.fallback if item.fallback is not None else fallback_oob_opt
                        if fb is not None:
                            resolved.append({'start':0, 'end':0, 'fallback':fb, 'raw':item.raw, 'is_range':False})
                        else:
                            err_msg = f"Error: Out of bounds: {item.raw}"
                            break
                    else:
                        resolved.append({'start':pos, 'end':pos, 'fallback':item.fallback, 'raw':item.raw, 'is_range':False})
                else:
                    left_val = item.left if item.left is not None else 1
                    right_val = item.right if item.right is not None else len(split['fields'])
                    left_pos = None
                    if item.left is None:
                        left_pos=1
                    else:
                        lv=left_val
                        if lv>0 and lv<=len(split['fields']):
                            left_pos=lv
                    right_pos = None
                    if item.right is None:
                        right_pos=len(split['fields'])
                    else:
                        rv=right_val
                        if rv>0 and rv<=len(split['fields']):
                            right_pos=rv
                        else:
                            right_pos=None
                    if left_pos is None:
                        fb = item.fallback if item.fallback is not None else fallback_oob_opt
                        if fb is not None:
                            resolved.append({'start':0, 'end':0, 'fallback':fb, 'raw':item.raw, 'is_range':True})
                            continue
                        else:
                            err_msg = f"Error: Out of bounds: {left_val}"
                            break
                    if right_pos is None:
                        # right OOB -> output clamped + error
                        if left_pos <= len(split['fields']):
                            resolved.append({'start':left_pos, 'end':len(split['fields']), 'fallback':item.fallback, 'raw':item.raw, 'is_range':True})
                        err_msg = f"Error: Out of bounds: {left_val}"
                        break
                    if left_pos > right_pos:
                        err_msg = f"Error: Field left value cannot be greater than right value"
                        break
                    resolved.append({'start':left_pos, 'end':right_pos, 'fallback':item.fallback, 'raw':item.raw, 'is_range':True})

            # build output with leading delim for -j
            line_out=''
            if join_flag==True or replace_opt is not None:
                jd = replace_opt if replace_opt is not None else delim_info['pattern']
                first=True
                for res in resolved:
                    if res['start']==0:
                        fb=res['fallback']
                        if first:
                            line_out+=fb
                            first=False
                        else:
                            line_out+=jd
                            line_out+=fb
                    elif res['is_range']:
                        slice_s = build_range_slice(split, res['start'], res['end'], replace_opt)
                        if first:
                            if res['start']==1:
                                line_out+=slice_s
                            else:
                                line_out+=jd
                                line_out+=slice_s
                            first=False
                        else:
                            line_out+=jd
                            line_out+=slice_s
                    else:
                        fv=split['fields'][res['start']-1]
                        if first:
                            if res['start']==1:
                                line_out+=fv
                            else:
                                line_out+=jd
                                line_out+=fv
                            first=False
                        else:
                            line_out+=jd
                            line_out+=fv
            else:
                for res in resolved:
                    if res['start']==0:
                        line_out+=res['fallback']
                    elif res['is_range']:
                        line_out+=build_range_slice(split, res['start'], res['end'], replace_opt)
                    else:
                        line_out+=split['fields'][res['start']-1]

            if line_out!='' or resolved:
                if zero_terminated:
                    sys.stdout.write(line_out)
                    sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'\x00')
                else:
                    sys.stdout.write(line_out)
